title: India come from behind to beat Japan 4-1 for record sixth Asian Champions Trophy title
dek: Japan led for more than 40 minutes in Mohali before goals from Shilanand Lakra, Dilpreet Singh, Jugraj Singh and Vivek Sagar Prasad sealed India's third straight title.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India won the men's Asian Champions Trophy for a record sixth time on Thursday, coming from a goal down to beat Japan 4-1 in the final in Mohali and retain the title they won in 2023 and 2024.

Japan, playing their first final in the competition since 2021, took the lead inside the first three minutes when Kazumasa Matsumoto beat two defenders and scored with a reverse shot past goalkeeper Suraj Karkera, The Bridge reported. They held that lead through the first half, and India did not win a penalty corner in the first quarter.

India equalised in the 42nd minute through Shilanand Lakra and then pulled away in the final quarter. Dilpreet Singh put them ahead in the 50th minute, Jugraj Singh converted a penalty corner in the 53rd and Vivek Sagar Prasad added the fourth in the 55th, according to Outlook India's live coverage. Midfielder Hardik Singh was playing his 200th international match.

India, who went unbeaten through the tournament, had beaten Japan 4-1 in the league stage in Jalandhar on 30 October and South Korea 8-1 in Wednesday's semi-final. It was the first time the two sides had met in an Asian Champions Trophy final.
